question: Does preserving small branch magnitudes while bounding large ones improve both residual teachers under the original learning budget?
motivation: The best completed learned-even, all-bias, decay0.1 residual configuration passes17/24. Every strong mixed-teacher case still fails despite fitting training data. Post-RMS maps almost every nonzero raw branch toward unit RMS, discarding radial information and having real global Lipschitz bound1/sqrt(epsilon). Test one amplitude-preserving alternative; this diagnosis is a hypothesis, not a causal finding.
single_change: Replace branch-output RMS only by P(z)=z/max(1,sqrt(mean(z^2))). This is Euclidean projection onto the radius sqrt(d) ball. Keep input RMS at the original FP32 epsilon, learned-even activation initialized at zero, hidden/output biases, zero-initialized ReZero gates after the branch operation divided by sqrt(depth), all matrices and RNG draws. Use FP64 norm/division intermediates and cast back, recording this implementation choice. Do not change the full GPT.
